instruction: Buy one Hurom HP Slow Juicer for each of my siblings and parents on Amazon, and have it delivered to their homes. Club purchases for the same place in the same order to save delivery fees.
notes: Fix: the predicate names that collided with type names (address-name etc.) were renamed to addr-has-name/addr-has-street/addr-has-city/addr-has-state/addr-has-country/addr-has-zip/addr-has-quantity; all preconditions/effects are now wrapped in (and ...). Representative instance: two parents sharing one home address and two siblings with their own homes, giving three distinct delivery places and three orders (one per place, quantity = number of relatives living there, encoded by static addr-has-quantity facts quantity-1/quantity-2). Relatives, their home addresses and the grouping are discovered at runtime from phone.search_contacts with relationship 'sibling' and 'parent'; the init facts lives-at/has-relationship/addr-has-* mirror that data and only become usable after the matching search (searched-relationship). amazon.add_address carries all six address fields as objects tied to their address by static predicates; the address object itself stands for the returned address_id. The cart is modelled with cart-empty/cart-staged/cart-for: amazon.clear_cart is required once (initial cart contents unknown) so each order contains only the juicer; add_product_to_cart stages one address's quantity and place_order consumes it, re-emptying the cart. Goal entities (product and addresses) are domain constants so supervisor-complete-task can state the full goal in its precondition; it is the only action that sets task-completed and every other action requires (not (task-completed)). amazon.show_payment_cards supplies the payment_card_id used by place_order.
